requirement: Configure a named logger with one formatted stream handler so that calling setup again replaces its own handler without touching others, accept case-insensitive level names, reject unknown names, default to INFO, and stop records from reaching the root logger.
skeleton: configure_logger resolving the level, removing and closing the previously installed named handler, adding a new StreamHandler with a fixed format, and disabling propagation.
caption: Repeatable setup for a standard-library logging.Logger. configure_logger(name, stream, level=logging.INFO) accepts either a numeric level or a level name; a name is upper-cased and looked up in logging.getLevelNamesMapping, and a name that is not found raises ValueError naming the unknown log level. It then walks a copy of the logger's handlers, removing and closing any handler whose name is the module's HANDLER_NAME, so calling setup twice leaves one handler writing to the newest stream while handlers installed by other code stay attached. A new logging.StreamHandler for the stream is named HANDLER_NAME, formatted as the level name, the logger name, a colon and the message, attached, and the logger's level is set. Propagation is switched off so the root logger's handlers never see these records. The fixture asserts that configuring twice writes INFO t108.replace: hello only to the second stream, that a foreign handler still receives a warning after two setups, that the default level hides debug and shows info, that the name debug enables a debug line, that the name loud raises ValueError, and that a handler on the root logger receives nothing.

plan.intent: Set up application logging safely more than once
constraints: Repeated setup leaves exactly one of its own handlers
Handlers added by other code are left in place
Level names are case insensitive and unknown names raise ValueError
Records do not propagate to the root logger

rationale.teaches: Tagging a handler with set_name so setup can find and replace exactly its own handler, plus explicit level resolution and propagate control.
rationale.why: Logging setup that runs twice, in tests or reloads, quietly doubles every line or wipes other libraries' handlers, and the damage only shows in captured output.

ops.docstring: Configure a named logger idempotently so repeated setup never duplicates output.

candidates.why_wrong: An unknown level name reaches setLevel as None and fails with a TypeError instead of a ValueError naming it.
The name test is inverted, so setup strips other code's handlers and keeps its own old one, writing every line twice.
The default level is WARNING, so info messages are dropped unless a level is passed.
Level names are lower-cased before the lookup, so every valid name is reported as unknown.
Propagation stays on, so root handlers receive every record as well.
